# tenferro v0.11.0

0.10.0 stopped identifying one body of content: the crates on crates.io were
built from `fd5fc73de6`, and `main` kept the `0.10.0` version string for the 49
commits that followed. v0.11.0 renumbers that tree and collects what those
commits change. The version number moves one minor because no compatibility
promise exists yet; a Rust caller should still read it as a breaking release.

## Breaking changes

### `set_placement` is fallible, and only on the `Dynamic` representation

`TypedTensor::set_placement` returns `crate::Result<()>` instead of `()`, and it
and `set_cpu_affinity` left `impl<T, R, D: Representation> TypedTensor<T, R, D>`,
so a `Host`- or `Gpu`-typed owner can no longer be relabelled. The payload
decides placement compatibility: `MemoryKind::Device` or `Managed` on a plain
host payload is now an error, which is the contradiction those two paths used to
disagree about. `is_host_memory()` is the one host/device predicate the rest of
the crate asks, and `Representation` gains `default_placement()`.

Migration: relabel through `into_dynamic()`, as in
`let mut t = host.into_dynamic(); t.set_placement(p)?;`.
`tests/ui/storage/fail/host_placement_is_not_settable.rs` pins the other half:
the compiler refuses `set_placement` on a `Host`-typed value (`E0599`).
([#2484](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2484), merged as
[#2497](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2497) and
[#2507](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2507))

### `tensor_view` and `tensor_read` return `Option`

`TensorRead::tensor_view`, `TensorValue::tensor_view` and
`TensorValue::tensor_read` answer `None` instead of aborting with
`unreachable!`: `tensor_view` for any `Tensor::external` payload, and
`tensor_read` only when the view layout differs from the stored tensor's
(`as_tensor` compares layouts, not compactness, so a reshaped external value
that still covers the whole buffer in a different layout has no read).
`TensorRead::as_slice` and the CPU engine's `download_to_host` /
`upload_host_tensor` report that case as `Error::UnsupportedDType` instead of
aborting.

Migration: `read.tensor_view()` becomes `read.tensor_view().ok_or(..)?`, or a
`match` on `Some(TensorView::..)`.
([#2486](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2486), merged as
[#2490](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2490))

### `dim_expr_to_sym_dim_public` is removed

`tenferro_runtime::dim_expr_to_sym_dim_public` (doc-hidden) turned a program's
`DimExpr::InputDim { input_idx, axis }` into
`SymDim::tensor_axis(input_idx as u64, axis)` — a value indistinguishable from
the axis of the traced handle whose id happens to be `input_idx`, so a
conversion given one read the other's axis. A program input position has no
meaning as a `SymDim`, and no public path produces one any more.

Migration, per extent:

- an extent that does not depend on inputs is
  `SymDim::from(expr.eval(&[])?)` (`DimExpr::eval`);
- a symbolic extent of a traced value is `TracedTensor::axis_sym_dim(axis)` (or
  `sym_shape()` / `sym_size(axis)`) on the handle that owns it — the program
  output, or the leaf returned by the `TraceContext::input_*` constructor of
  that input.

([#2443](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2443), merged as
[#2473](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2473))

### `SvdDriver` and `EighDriver` name an algorithm family

`SvdDriver::{Gesvdj, Gesvd, Xgesvdp}` became `{Jacobi, QrBased, Polar}`, and
`EighDriver::{Syevd, Syevj}` became `{DivideAndConquer, Jacobi}`.
`Auto` and every derivation are unchanged; the variant docs now state the
efficacy and keep one line naming the routine the CUDA provider maps the family
to. This is a source-breaking rename of public enum variants.
([#2516](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2516), merged as
[#2517](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2517))

### The `rocm` placeholder feature is gone

The unused `rocm` feature left `tenferro-gpu` and the five crates that forwarded
it (`tenferro-ad`, `tenferro-einsum`, `tenferro-fft`, `tenferro-linalg`,
`tenferro-internal-ops`): no code was gated on it and HIP/ROCm has no
implementation. A consumer that enabled or forwarded `rocm` drops it from its
feature list ([#2310](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/issues/2310),
merged as [#2470](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2470)).

### `TensorView` and `TensorViewMut` gained a representation parameter

Both carry a defaulted `D: Representation = Dynamic`. A type annotation still
names the same type, but the `Host` specialization adds its own inherent
`dtype`, so an associated-function reference such as `TensorView::dtype` is now
`E0034` ambiguous: name the representation
(`TensorView::<Dynamic>::dtype`).

### Dependency moves

[#2494](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2494) moved the workspace
onto the `threadteam` 0.5 line;
[#2521](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2521) moved it onto the
`t4a-faer` 0.33 chain, which is one release train because `tcontract-exec`,
`cpueinsum` and `tlinalg` all pin `t4a-faer` themselves.

| dependency | 0.10.0 | 0.11.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `threadteam` | 0.4.0 | 0.5.1 |
| `strided-basic`, `-perm`, `-kernel`, `-fused`, `-nn` | 0.11.0 | 0.12.0 |
| `strided-view` | 0.7.0 | 0.7.1 |
| `t4a-faer` | 0.30.0 | 0.33.0 |
| `tcontract-exec` | 0.10.0 | 0.12.0 |
| `tlinalg` | 0.9.0 | 0.11.0 |
| `cpueinsum`, `cpueinsum-blas` | 0.10.0 | 0.12.0 |
| `t4a-cuda-kernels` | `=0.1.1` (rev `b429d41`) | `=0.1.2` (rev `ab7395c`) |

`strided-traits` (0.7.0), `tlinalg-blas` (0.5.1) and `t4a-cuda-runtime` (0.1.0)
are unchanged. Two generations now cross the crate boundary: an `Exec` carries a
`threadteam` 0.5 `TeamExec`, so the pool, the token and the `Exec` a host builds
must come from the same generation, and `CpuBatchPolicy`, `CpuBatchStrategy` and
`CpuBatchThresholds` (re-exports of `tcontract_exec` types) move with
`tcontract-exec` 0.12. Two copies in one graph are `E0308`.

Nothing was removed from the linalg factorization surface itself
([#2483](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2483), merged as
[#2481](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2481),
[#2506](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2506) and
[#2508](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2508)): that change is
additive, and the engine entries keep their signatures while running the same
typed bodies.

## Results that can differ in the final bit

Two changes pick a different algorithm, so the same call can return different
last bits than it did on 0.10.0. Neither is pinned by a bit-equality test.

- A serial `native` c64 contraction takes faer on every host class again
  ([#2524](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2524), merged as
  [#2526](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2526)). 0.10.0 had
  narrowed 0.9.0's rule to `(X86_64Avx2, 1)`, which left every other
  `HostClass` on tcontract's packed driver at a thread budget of one above
  `m*n*k = 1 << 17`, with no measurement behind the exception (1.28x to 1.45x
  slower per call in the reported downstream workload). A budget of one now
  lifts the c64 bound on all six classes, and the test reaches the list through
  an exhaustive `match`. The two drivers do not accumulate in the same order;
  the test asserts which driver is selected and the performance note beside it
  cites a normwise bound, not bit equality. Wider budgets keep the default.
- `t4a-cuda-kernels` 0.1.2 changes reduction numerics
  ([#2534](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2534)). Split pass 1
  now assigns lanes by group instead of per lane, so `sum` and `sum_squares`
  over a contiguous axis accumulate `f32`/`f64` partials in a different order.
  The NaN-propagating extrema are rewritten as selects, a near-overflow fold
  (`x0=x1=A`, `x32=x33=-A`, `A = 2^127`) that returned 0 now returns NaN, and
  the kernel ABI revision moves from 12 to 13 (no symbol, signature, struct or
  launch-geometry change).

## Improvements

- `TraceContextLinalgExt` and `TraceContextFftExt` give the linalg and fft
  families the `TraceContext` entry point the other families already had: the
  context method takes the context's `TraceValue` inputs with a `&self`
  receiver, and the existing `TracedTensorLinalgExt` / `TracedTensorFftExt`
  methods delegate to it in one line, so both spellings record the same
  operations. Both are re-exported from their crate preludes. Additive.
  ([#2525](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2525), merged as
  [#2531](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2531))
- `tenferro_tensor::capability_entry` is the one lookup rule behind
  `TensorBackendCapability::capability` and `::require_capability`: backend id,
  operation, dtype and the optional capability axis are matched in one place, so
  a kernel that needs to know whether its table admits a dtype calls the same
  code the trait does. `CpuEngine`'s analytic dtype gate now goes through it.
  ([#2483](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2483))
- One host narrowing for borrowed reads — `TensorRead::try_host(op)`,
  `TensorView::try_host(op)` and `TypedTensorView::try_host(op)`. Each returns a
  host-marked view when the read borrows host elements, and otherwise a
  `RuntimeState` error naming `op` (backend storage) or an `UnsupportedDType`
  error naming `op` (a `Tensor::external` payload). The host-marked views widen
  back without copying (`into_dynamic`), and `TensorView<'_, Host>` reports
  `dtype`, `shape` and `is_owned_layout`.
- The same narrowing for write targets — `TensorWrite::try_mut_host(op)`,
  `TensorViewMut::try_mut_host(op)` and `TypedTensorViewMut::try_mut_host(op)`
  ([#2499](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2499)). Each returns a
  host-marked mutable view with the read side's errors. A valid placement
  label is preserved, not rewritten: the native constructors and
  `set_placement` reject Device/Managed on host storage, while a tensor built
  through `Tensor::external_with_placement` keeps whatever label it was given
  and still reports `is_host_memory() == true`.
  `TensorViewMut<'_, Host>` reports `dtype`, `shape` and `strides`.
- `tenferro_linalg::error::map_error` is public
  ([#2462](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2462)): it is the
  translation tenferro's own linalg entries apply to a `tlinalg` failure, so a
  caller that runs `tlinalg` factorizations itself reports the same error
  instead of copying a variant table. Each `tlinalg::Error` variant maps to one
  documented tenferro variant and kind, a variant a later `tlinalg` adds becomes
  `Error::Internal` with its `Debug` text, and it never panics. Available with
  the `native` or `blas` feature.
- Borrowed-`Exec` factorization entries with typed outputs:
  `svd_with_exec`, `svd_values_with_exec`, `qr_with_exec`, `eigh_with_exec`,
  `eigh_values_with_exec` and `eig_values_with_exec` (`native` only). They run
  on a caller's `Exec` bundle and `BufferPool`, read a `[m, n]` or batched
  `[m, n, b..]` view in place (a negative stride is `Unsupported`), take every
  output and workspace from that pool, and return singular values and Hermitian
  eigenvalues in `LinalgScalar::RealScalar`, general eigenvalues in
  `LinalgScalar::Complex`. The engine entries run the same functions and only
  erase the results, so both give bit-identical outputs.
  `LinalgScalar` gains `RealScalar`, and its `Complex` now also implements
  `PoolScalar + Default`
  ([#2462](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2462)).
- The CPU complex SVD and `eigh` lease the real spectrum from the session pool
  instead of a fresh `Vec`, and the ceiling `cpu_linalg_allocation` asserts for
  `faer/svd/complex32` and `faer/eigh/complex32` is 1 allocation. The guarantee is
  about that buffer and about payloads and workspace, not about every byte a
  call touches: the engine entries that erase typed outputs into a `Vec<Tensor>`
  still build that vector on the ordinary heap
  (`svd_erased`/`pair_erased` in `crates/tenferro-linalg/src/cpu/backend.rs`), and
  a returned tensor's dims and strides are shape metadata, inline up to
  `INLINE_RANK` (8) axes and heap-allocated above that. The `blas` route keeps the
  spectrum real instead of widening it.
  ([#2462](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2462)).
- CUDA reductions cost about 20 µs less per standalone call: `tenferro-gpu`
  reductions wait once per call instead of once per pass plus once more for the
  result squeeze, write the squeezed result directly, and no longer zero-fill
  destinations their kernels overwrite completely. In the paired A100 run
  reported in #2474 (raw samples were not archived and are not re-measured
  here), 1M
  full-reduce cells moved from 47-55 µs to 27-35 µs, bit-identically; rank >
  `MAX_RANK` keeps the general path ([#2406](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2406)).

## Behavior changes

- `is_host_memory()` on `TypedTensor`, its views, `Tensor`, `TensorRead`,
  `TensorWrite` and `TensorViewMut` is the one host/device answer. The payload
  decides — a plain host owner, a host slice and a CPU-resident allocation group
  are host memory, a backend buffer is not — and `Placement::memory_kind` never
  does. `try_host`, `try_mut_host`, the CPU provider's operand admission and
  linalg's borrowed entries all run this one predicate, so a tensor can no
  longer be host memory to linalg and device memory to the CPU provider.
- `TypedTensor::into_host` makes `Host` evidence rather than a hint: it does
  not rewrite the label. The narrow keeps `PinnedHost` / `UnpinnedHost` and
  any `cpu_affinity`; a plain host payload cannot carry `Device` or `Managed`
  (construction and relabelling reject those), and `Other(label)` is kept.
- `TensorLayout::validate_mutable_no_overlap` runs
  `strided_view::is_injective_layout`, the analysis that already guards
  strided-rs' own mutable kernels, and `tenferro-tensor-core` depends on
  `strided-view` for it. The local stride-span proof and its 4096-element
  exact-enumeration ceiling are gone, so an injective interleaved layout such as
  `[3, 1500]` with strides `[2000, 3]` is accepted for writing instead of being
  reported as `OverlappingMutableLayout`. Genuinely overlapping layouts still get
  that error, and an element count that does not fit `usize` still gets
  `IntegerOverflow` ([#2484](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2484)).
- `sum`, sum of squares and `prod` accept a zero-length reduced axis and return
  the fold's own unit: `reduce_sum` / `reduce_prod` on a `[0, 2]` input over axis
  0 now yields `[2]` filled with `0` / `1` instead of `InvalidArgument`, on the
  owned and borrowed-view CPU entries and on the CUDA entries, for every dtype
  the fold supports (`F32`, `F64`, complex, `I32`, `I64`). `max` and `min` keep
  the typed `InvalidArgument` when the kept shape is nonempty: they have no
  finite identity, and reporting a sentinel would invent a value the input never
  held; if a kept dimension is also zero, the CUDA entry returns the empty
  result before that check. An empty axis list still returns the input unchanged
  for `sum` and `prod`; sum of squares returns the squared input instead
  ([#2453](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2453)).
- `rem` differentiates away from its discontinuities in the semantic AD
  transforms: `linearize` emits `dx - trunc(x / y) * dy` and the reverse rule
  emits `1` and `-trunc(x / y)` times the cotangent, with `trunc(x / y)` built
  in the core vocabulary as `q - rem(q, 1)`, without a separate primitive. The
  graph and the primal can disagree when `x / y` rounds across an integer, so
  the emitted quotient is the rounded one. The derivative is undefined at
  `y == 0` and at a nonzero integer quotient; `x == 0` is differentiable
  (`rem(x, y) == x` near it); those single points are left out rather than
  given a one-sided value
  ([#2454](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2454)).
- The CPU linalg and reduction entries narrow each operand to `Host` once and no
  longer re-check placement below that point: the `ensure_host_tensor` /
  `ensure_host_tensor_read` pre-checks (56 call sites in `tenferro-linalg`, 5 in
  `tenferro-cpu`) and the helpers are removed, and every `LinalgBackend` method
  and reduction entry calls `try_host` at its boundary. A backend-buffer operand
  is still refused with `RuntimeState`. One behaviour difference: a borrowed
  view that already covers its buffer in compact column-major order is no longer
  copied before a non-faer linalg route. A native host payload cannot carry a
  device or managed label (construction and `set_placement` reject it);
  `Tensor::external_with_placement` keeps the caller's label and still reports
  host memory, and `into_host` moves the payload without relabelling it.
- The BLAS-provider lane boundary is documented in the CPU execution and
  backend-choice guides and on the `TensorDot` entries of `CpuEngine`: a vendor
  call takes the whole engine and the library's own threads, so a context budget
  is not honoured there, lanes must not enter the vendor provider concurrently
  unless the library tolerates it, and only the native provider has a
  per-context entry
  ([#2463](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2463)).
- The CUDA allocation pool now keeps freed blocks within
  `clamp(total_memory / 8, 256 MiB, 4 GiB)` per runtime instead of a fixed
  256 MiB (`crates/tenferro-gpu/src/cuda/runtime.rs:208-239`). A working set that
  fits that budget no longer re-maps memory on every call while the runtime
  is retained; on a device whose eighth of memory is at or below 256 MiB the budget
  is unchanged, and a working set above 4 GiB still exceeds it.
  `TENFERRO_CUDA_POOL_RELEASE_MIB` overrides the budget (also clamped to the same
  range), `CudaRuntime::pool_release_threshold_bytes()` reports it, and
  `CudaRuntime::trim_pool(keep_bytes)` returns idle pool memory above
  `keep_bytes` to the driver
  ([#2398](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2398)).

## Fixes

- A borrowed linalg entry refuses an empty operand with a negative stride: the
  six `*_with_exec` factorizations validated the layout inside `raw_view`, which
  the zero-dimension shortcut returned before, so a `[3, 0]` or `[0, 0]` view
  whose remaining axis was reversed came back with empty outputs while the same
  layout on a non-empty operand was `Unsupported`. The stride rule now runs
  before the shortcut, so the empty operand fails with the non-empty error,
  variant and message included
  ([#2505](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2505)).
- The borrowed entries' storage guarantee is scoped to the payload and the
  workspace: a view's and an output's dims and strides are shape metadata,
  inline up to `INLINE_RANK` (8) axes and heap-allocated above that, so a rank-9
  operand allocates a few small metadata blocks per call. The contract says what
  it covers, and `tests/cpu_linalg_allocation.rs` carries a rank-8 row (no
  allocations) beside a rank-9 row (some)
  ([#2505](https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/pull/2505)).
- The serial `native` c64 contraction rule is restored on every host class; see
  [Results that can differ in the final bit](#results-that-can-differ-in-the-final-bit)
  for the numerics this changes.

**Full comparison:** https://github.com/tensor4all/tenferro-rs/compare/v0.10.0...v0.11.0
